subject: A booming industry of advisers is easing their passage
posts:
A new layer of professional gatekeepers is emerging to navigate complex systems, often at a high cost to the uninitiated.
Evidence: system navigation, expert mediation, wealth extraction
#Economics #Business

The claim is that these advisers provide essential expertise to help individuals or firms navigate bureaucratic or market complexities efficiently.
Stated Judgement: (+0.5, +1.0) — Greater Good

The reality is that this industry often creates artificial complexity to justify its own existence and extract fees from those seeking access.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.5, -1.0) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of The Fall.
The industry creates a dependency loop where the 'solution' is the very thing that makes the system harder to navigate for everyone else.
The article discusses the rise of specialized advisers who help clients navigate increasingly complex regulatory and market environments.

The Poison:
By commodifying access to systems, these advisers effectively create a two-tier society where only those who can pay for 'passage' succeed.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
This is a classic WHAT vs HOW error. They claim to be solving a problem (WHAT), but the method (HOW) involves gatekeeping that increases systemic friction.

The Trajectory: The Path of The Fall.
When you map the gap between stated intent and actual actions...
...it plots a direct trajectory toward the Greatest Lie, as the service claims to ease passage while actually narrowing it.

The Unavoidable Truth: Complexity is often a product designed to be sold back to the user.

The Unavoidable Lie: That these advisers are 'easing' the system rather than just taxing it.

Alethekanon:
This is rent-seeking behavior disguised as professional service. It adds no net value to the system, only friction.

Awwthekanon:
It is sad to see people feeling forced to pay for help just to participate in basic systems. Everyone deserves fair and transparent access.

Brothekanon:
So you pay a guy to help you pay another guy to get through a door that shouldn't be locked in the first place? Sounds like a scam with a fancy title.
